title: 2007 AMC 12B 17
statement: If \(a\) is a nonzero integer and \(b\) is a positive number such that \(ab^2=\log_{10}b,\) what is the median of the set \(\{0,1,a,b,\frac{1}{b}\}?\)

solutions.text:
For \(b\gt0,\) we have \(b\lt10^b,\) hence \(\log_{10}b\lt b.\) If \(b=1,\) then \(a=0.\) If \(b\gt1,\) then \(0\lt\dfrac{\log_{10}b}{b^2}\lt1,\) so \(a\) could not be an integer.

Hence \(0\lt b\lt1,\) so \(\log_{10}b\lt0\) and \(a=\dfrac{\log_{10}b}{b^2}\lt0.\) Thus \(a\lt0\lt b\lt1\lt\dfrac1b,\) and the middle value of the sorted set is \(b.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Since \(b\lt10^b\) for all \(b\gt0,\) we have \(\log_{10}b\lt b\)
Rule out \(b\ge1\) by checking whether \(a=\dfrac{\log_{10}b}{b^2}\) can be a nonzero integer
